840: A whole city just rolled out beneath the window. It doesn't roll back up. Might as well visit.
841: Boarding call. Everyone stands up at once, as if standing sooner makes the plane leave sooner. Join them.
842: You've arrived, gently exhausted and mostly determined. Two out of two, honestly.
843: Wheels down, mind up, and one earbud still in from a song that ended an hour ago.
844: New city, new door handles, new light switches on the wrong side. Adventure includes furniture.
845: The captain said we've begun our descent, and your stomach agreed, loudly and right on time.
846: Every trip starts the same way: with a stranger's elbow and a strong sense of purpose.
847: You stretched, yawned, and stepped into a city that has never once heard of your bedtime.
848: Solid ground at last. Your legs were folded up for hours and are still filing a formal complaint about it.
849: Boarding soon. You've got your bag, your notes, and one sock you're fairly sure matches.
850: The window seat gave you clouds, then rooftops, then this. Say hello to this.
851: You arrived slightly early, which means you get to stand around looking capable. Enjoy.
852: New time zone, new streets, and a body that firmly believes it's still yesterday.
853: Off the plane, down the hallway, past the shops selling things nobody needs until exactly right now.
854: You made it. The suitcase made it. Somewhere, a thief did not expect either of you.
855: The engines went quiet and the whole city got a little louder to make up for it.
856: You packed snacks for a two-hour flight and ate them all in the first ten minutes. Impressive, really.
857: New airport chairs, same impossible armrests. You'll be standing anyway. Places to be.
858: The trip was long, the coffee was small, and the city ahead is enormous. Fair trade.
859: You stepped outside, where the taxi line welcomed you with the warmth of a very long queue and no taxis.
860: They demanded my finest office, sat in my chair, and asked when I would be bringing them coffee.
861: They wanted the largest account we offer, and then asked if we had one even larger.
862: They asked for a tour of the vault, and looked disappointed that it was merely full of money.
863: They introduced themselves with six important names, none of which I have ever heard of.
864: They insisted on meeting me privately, then spent the meeting admiring their own reflection.
865: They asked to speak to whoever runs the bank, and seemed unhappy to learn it was only me.
866: They opened an account, closed it, and opened a far grander one, mainly to keep three of us running after them.
867: They requested a chair grander than mine, and I quietly wished I had one to give them.
868: They wanted the vault opened just so they could stand inside and sigh with satisfaction.
869: They signed the forms with a signature so large it needed a second page.
870: They asked for our most exclusive account, then asked what would make it feel more exclusive.
871: They arrived without an appointment and behaved as though the appointment had been waiting for them.
872: They toured the vault, complimented our gold, and asked why we kept such wealth locked away.
873: They asked how many people I manage, then decided the number was far too small for someone like them.
874: They wanted a private meeting, a private room, and a private round of applause when they entered.
875: They read our list of top clients aloud and were genuinely hurt to find their own name missing from it.
876: They asked to see the biggest account in the building, then asked to be introduced to its owner.
877: They demanded the executive floor, admired the view, and asked if the whole thing could be theirs by evening.
878: They wanted every door opened for them, including the ones we normally keep firmly shut.
879: They spent an hour explaining how important they were, and left before I could learn their name.
